{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that age-related differences in preferences for work activities (specifically, the preference for helping colleagues over future-oriented activities) would be eliminated under conditions where time horizons are expanded.",
  "design": "mixed, with age as a continuous predictor and time horizon condition (unspecified, expanded, limited) as a between-subjects factor.",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Experimental manipulation of occupational time horizons via written prompts: participants were asked to imagine either that they had unscheduled time (unspecified), that the company wanted them to stay considerably longer (expanded), or that their contract was expiring soon (limited).",
  "outcome_measure": "Forced-choice between three work-related activities: 'Help a colleague or a friend with a company project' (emotionally meaningful), 'Work on a project that may help you advance your career' (future-oriented), or 'Work on a project that may lead the company in a new direction' (future-oriented).",
  "population_and_setting": "Employed adults recruited via KnowledgePanel of GfK Research in the United States.",
  "sample_size_total": 555,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited from a larger study about decisions and regret; no specific incentive for this task mentioned beyond participation in the larger study.",
  "analysis_plan": "Logistic regression to test the association between age and the likelihood of choosing to help a colleague versus future-oriented activities, including the interaction between age and experimental condition.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used an adapted version of the social partner paradigm. The two future-oriented options were collapsed into a single category for the primary analysis. Control variables included Future Time Perspective, education, and personality traits."
}
